title: Revitalised National Competition Policy
summary: Treasurers agreed a revitalised National Competition Policy on 29 November 2024 and more reforms on 28 November 2025 (zoning, standards, occupational licensing, heavy vehicles, right to repair). Individual reforms have no commencement dates yet.

instruments.title: Federation Funding Agreement Schedule on the National Competition Policy

direction_rationale: A package of state reforms to zoning, standards and licensing with federal payments for delivery.
comparison: States adopting individual reforms at different times
notes: Not yet a regulatory change. Each state reform should get its own record when it is legislated.

assessment.summary: Commonwealth, state and territory treasurers agreed a revitalised National Competition Policy, with payments for reforms to zoning, standards, occupational licensing, heavy vehicles and the right to repair. The Productivity Commission's modelling puts the gains from a wider package at 1.0 to 1.7% of GDP. Not yet in force.

marks.reason: Aligning standards with international ones and national licensing for some occupations integrate markets.
Zoning and planning reform lowers barriers to new businesses and housing.
Occupational licensing reform eases moves between states and occupations.
Right to repair and modern methods of construction ease adoption of better technology.

assessment.confidence_note: Marks reflect the agreed reform areas; they depend on what each government delivers.

responsible.note: Its matters include competition policy and Commonwealth-State financial relations.
